input.quote: The exclusive remedy of either party in a claim against the other under this Agreement shall be the recovery of its direct damages. In no event shall either party be liable to the other for the recovery of any special, indirect or consequential damages even if the defendant party had been advised of the possibility of such damages including but not limited to lost profits, lost revenues, failure to realize expected savings, loss of data and loss of use. ... The limitation of liability in this Section 15 shall not apply to breaches of Sections 13 and 14.
input.rationale: Despite the one-sided heading ("Limitation of Garman's Liability"), Section 15 operates mutually: the direct-damages remedy and the exclusion of special, indirect and consequential damages both apply to "either party", and the limitation is disapplied for breaches of Section 13 (intellectual property) and Section 14 (confidentiality) — i.e. our two principal areas of exposure sit outside it. Critically, there is no monetary cap anywhere in the Agreement (search for aggregate/cap/exceed language returns nothing), so Garman's liability for direct damages is uncapped. That is better for us than the preferred position of a cap at the greater of 12 months' fees and USD 1,000,000, and there is no one-way cap protecting only the Vendor and no statement that our liability is unlimited while Garman's is capped. Our own direct-damages exposure is likewise uncapped, but adding the playbook cap here would principally benefit Garman by limiting our recovery, so we do not redline. Two sub-elements short of preferred, noted only: the carve-outs do not expressly name gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud (Sections 13 and 14 already cover IP and confidentiality), and there is no statement that our payment obligations are not "damages" for these purposes.
